headline: Indian Markets Mixed as IT and Tata Stocks Drag Sensex Down
why: Higher US Treasury yields weighing on global risk sentiment.
Global investor sentiment dropping to a 16-month low per recent surveys.
Weakness in IT majors and select Tata group heavyweights dragging indices.
Uncertainty surrounding global crude oil trends and mixed Asian market cues.
whatHappening: Nifty shows resilience while Sensex dips due to weakness in key sectors.
Paytm remains in focus following opening trade queries and market volatility.
SBI projects FCNR(B) deposits could yield ₹5 trillion in notional profits for banks.
Air India considers merging its budget unit into the group to optimize operational costs.

stocksInNews.sources: In focus as traders monitor market opening volatility and sentiment
Projected FCNR(B) deposit profits to boost banking sector earnings
Broad IT sector weakness and pressure on Tata group stocks
Overall Tata group weakness contributing to Sensex decline
Drag from US market tech sell-off and higher yield environment
Steady institutional interest helping stabilize the Nifty index
Favorable banking sector outlook on forex deposit profit projections
Tracking global crude oil movements and broader GIFT Nifty cues
Defensive interest as investors seek stability amid mixed market trends
Capital goods strength providing underlying support to broader markets

summary: Indian equities traded on a mixed note today, with Nifty holding steady while the Sensex slipped due to drag in IT and Tata group stocks. Global markets face headwinds from rising US Treasury yields and low investor sentiment, alongside shifting crude oil prices. Key domestic highlights include strong profit projections for banks on FCNR deposits and strategic consolidation plans in the aviation sector.
